text:
Marathon Petroleum edged up 0.31% today to close at $388.90, capping a strong two-week rally of 7.81%. The stock has benefited from a combination of tight refining conditions: refineries are running at 98% capacity, diesel prices hit record highs this week as Ukraine and Iran conflicts knocked refineries offline, and U.S. crude is trading at $91.48 per barrel. These constraints tighten margins for refiners that can keep running, rewarding companies like this one with higher profits on fuel sales.

The broader tailwind is a tightening global energy market. Russia's ban on diesel exports, the closure of refineries due to ongoing conflicts, and now coordination between the U.S., EU, and South Korea on sanctions against Iran all point to sustained pressure on energy supply. A major new oil supply source from Venezuela under the Trump administration (announced yesterday) could eventually ease some of this pressure, but for now the refining sector faces sustained demand with constrained supply — a profitable backdrop for U.S. refiner margins over the coming months.
